title: Operation “Good Neighbor”: the IDF brought thousands of wounded and sick Syrians to Israel for treatment

trailer.text: The IDF said it has a “moral imperative” to provide aid to the Syrians on Israel’s northern border.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the IDF began treating wounded and sick Syrians in 2013, and the treatment was provided free of charge.
According to the IDF, over 4,000 people were brought to Israel for medical treatment, among them hundreds of children.
Food, tents, generators and fuel were also transferred to Syria, and the operation ended in 2018, when the Assad government regained control of southern Syria.

glance.label: Since
glance.value: Treatment of the wounded from 2013, the operation from June 2016

glance.label: Where
glance.value: The Syrian border in the Golan Heights

glance.label: Scale
glance.value: Over 4,000 Syrians treated in Israel, according to the IDF

paragraphs.text: According to the article in Ynet in Hebrew, about 250 thousand people lived beyond the fence, and their lives were affected by the chaos of the civil war.
On the Syrian side of the border there was a severe shortage of medical infrastructure, doctors and medicines.
Israel largely tried to stay out of the war in Syria.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the IDF began treating wounded and sick Syrians in 2013.
Yair Golan said that one night six stretchers were placed at the fence, and as a result the wounded were brought into Ziv hospital.
There are two versions of who approved bringing in the wounded.
The medical treatment was provided free of charge.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the IDF launched Operation Good Neighbor in June 2016, to increase aid to Syrian civilians without becoming involved in the war.
The IDF announced the operation and said it has a “moral imperative” to provide aid to the Syrians on the country’s northern border.
The civilians waited at a meeting point on the border.
Northern Command medical teams met them, began treatment immediately and evacuated them to hospitals.
According to the IDF, since the first activity more than 110 aid operations were carried out.
Eyal Dror headed the “Good Neighbor” directorate.
Marco Moreno, a lieutenant colonel in the reserves, is described as the founder of the project.
Moreno said that Israel has an explicit interest, and that it asked the Syrians not to allow terrorists to harm it.
A senior IDF officer said that the project has a significant impact on Israel’s security.

stations.title: In the hospitals in the north

paragraphs.text: The IDF brought to Israel, among others, six wounded Syrians, four of them children who were reportedly orphaned, for treatment in a hospital in the north.
The patients were treated anonymously, out of fear that they and their families would be harmed in Syria.
The hospital allowed journalists to see patients only on condition that last names not be published and that the patients be photographed from behind.
According to a representative of the Galilee Medical Center, more than 2,200 wounded Syrians were treated there since 2013, 40% of them women and children.
A 29-year-old patient, who was missing half of his face, was hospitalized for over a year for facial reconstruction surgery.
Hani, a Syrian refugee from Ghouta, is staying at the hospital in the Western Galilee, and has even learned some Hebrew.
He said he was asked if he wanted treatment in Israel, and immediately answered yes.
A military police soldier said that some of the wounded said thank you in Hebrew and expressed appreciation for having been saved.

stations.title: “Mazor Ladach”: a clinic in a military post

paragraphs.text: Israel operated “Mazor Ladach”, a field clinic in an unused military post, in the southern Golan Heights on the Syrian border.

Smiling soldiers brought dozens of mothers with their children into Israel for free medical care as part of Operation "Good Neighbor", and from there they were taken by bus to the Galilee Medical Center in Nahariya.
According to Brig. Gen. Asor, over 600 children and their parents came to Israel every month for medical treatment.
According to Eyal Dror, the largest project involved some 1,400 children with chronic illnesses, aged one month to 15.
A Syrian doctor who accompanied children to treatment in Israel said he is torn between helping the children and the risk to his life, but will continue to help.
In October, a volunteer doctor working at the field clinic was hit by a stray bullet from fighting across the border.
The clinic closed in August 2018.
According to the IDF, the quantity of food sent to Syria increased tenfold: from a few dozen tons between 2013 and 2016, to 360 tons in 2016–2017.
According to the IDF, some 1,700 tons of food, around 630 tents, 40 vehicles, 20 generators and 20 mobile structures were transferred to southern Syria.
Fuel was also transferred to Syria.
The aid sent across the border was labeled in Hebrew, and came from Israeli companies.
According to the army, most of the aid was donated by NGOs, and some was provided directly by the Israeli government.

stations.title: The end, the count and what the Syrians said

paragraphs.text: The IDF announced the end of Operation Good Neighbor, after Assad returned to control almost all of the country’s territory.
The announcement was made on September 13, 2018.
On July 22, the IDF rescued 800 White Helmets members and their family members, who were in imminent danger, from southern Syria.
According to the IDF, as of July 2017 more than 4,000 people had been brought to Israel for medical treatment, among them hundreds of children.
Different sources give different numbers.
The Northern Command’s chief medical officer said that the treatment of the Syrian neighbors is one of the most significant efforts he has ever witnessed.
A Syrian refugee named Said said that the Israeli side took a noble stance, in its aid and in treating the wounded.
Many Syrians who were made homeless expressed open gratitude to Israel.
A Syrian mother said that she used to see Israel as an occupying power, and no longer does.
Hani said that the Israelis are the only ones who did not close the border.
Golan said that Syrians told him they had thought Israel was the devil, and that it is saving lives.

According to the Jerusalem Report, years of Israeli humanitarian efforts have eroded the traditional image of Israel as an enemy in the eyes of Syrians, at least in the areas closest to the border with Israel.
Yossi Kuperwasser said that the Syrian public knows today that Israel tried to help it, at least on the humanitarian level.
Dror said that a Muslim Syrian sat in a Jewish synagogue in Canada and listened to his lecture.

stations.title: The border remained closed to refugees

paragraphs.text: A medical officer in the Bashan Division said that Israel’s policy is that the refugees stay on their side of the border and are not allowed to enter.
The IDF announced that it would not allow Syrian refugees into Israeli territory.
Defense Minister Liberman said that Israel is prepared to provide humanitarian assistance to civilians, women and children.
In mid-July, about 200 refugees waving white flags approached the border, apparently requesting asylum in Israel.
Israeli officials turned them away and said they would not be allowed to enter.
A military police soldier said that all the wounded declared that they had fought against the Assad regime, but there was no way to know if this was true.
He also said that they received an instruction to protect the wounded from Druze, out of fear of revenge, and that there was a case of assault.
According to a Wall Street Journal report, Israel secretly provided aid to Syrian rebels in the Golan for several years.
Israel has also in the past downplayed the extent of the assistance it provided to civilians on the border.
Dror said that cynics will say the suffering was exploited, but Israel chose to invest resources and risk lives for humanitarian aid.
Kuperwasser warned that this would not significantly change daily affairs on the border, which would go back to being closed.
With Assad’s retaking of the area in 2018, the directorate’s activity came to an end.

claims.quote: Over 4,000 people have been brought to Israel to receive medical treatment, among them hundreds of children, the IDF said.

claims.text: פליט סורי בשם סעיד אמר שהצד הישראלי נקט עמדה אצילית, הן בסיוע והן בטיפול בפצועים.
claims.quote: We saw a very noble stance by the Israeli side, both by the aid that it sent and in its treating of the wounded

claims.text: אם סורית סיפרה שבעבר ראתה בישראל כוח כובש אך כבר לא.
claims.quote: I used to see Israel as an occupying power,” she related as we waited for a doctor to call her son's name

claims.text: האני אמר שהישראלים הם היחידים שלא סגרו את הגבול.
claims.quote: The Israelis are the only ones who didn't close the border.

claims.text: גולן סיפר שסורים אמרו לו שחשבו שישראל היא השטן ושהיא מצילה חיים.
claims.quote: הרבה מהם אמרו לי 'חשבנו שאתם השטן, והנה אתם מצילים חיים'

claims.text: לפי הכתבה, שנים של מאמצים הומניטריים ישראליים שחקו את דימוי ישראל כאויב בעיני סורים.
claims.quote: Yet years of Israeli humanitarian efforts have eroded the traditional image of Israel as an enemy in the minds of Syrians

claims.text: יוסי קופרווסר אמר שהציבור הסורי יודע היום שישראל ניסתה לעזור לו לפחות ברמה ההומניטרית בשנות המלחמה.
claims.quote: Today, the Syrian public knows that Israel is a power that tried to help it, at least on the humanitarian level, during years of war.

claims.text: דרור סיפר שסורי מוסלמי ישב בבית כנסת יהודי בקנדה והאזין להרצאתו.
claims.quote: הוא היה מוסלמי, בתוך בית כנסת יהודי, שפשוט ישב ושמע אותי מרצה

claims.text: קצין רפואה בדיוויזיית הבשן אמר שמדיניות ישראל היא שהפליטים יישארו בצד שלהם של הגבול ולא יורשו להיכנס.
claims.quote: Our policy is that they should stay on their side of the border and that we will not let them enter

claims.text: צה"ל הודיע שלא יתיר לפליטים סורים להיכנס לשטח ישראל ויפעל להגנה על האינטרסים הביטחוניים של ישראל.
claims.quote: The IDF will not allow Syrian refugees into Israeli territory and will continue to act to protect Israel’s security interests

claims.text: שר הביטחון ליברמן אמר שישראל מוכנה לספק סיוע הומניטרי לאזרחים, נשים וילדים.

claims.quote: About 200 refugees approached the border in mid-July, waving white flags and apparently requesting asylum in Israel.

claims.quote: כולם הצהירו שהם לחמו נגד משטר אסד, אבל לא הייתה לנו דרך לדעת כמה זה נכון

claims.text: החייל סיפר שקיבלו הנחיה לשמור על הפצועים מפני דרוזים בשל חשש מנקמה, ושאירע מקרה של תקיפה.
claims.quote: קיבלנו הנחיה לשמור עליהם מפני דרוזים, כי חלקם לחמו בדרוזים בסוריה והיה חשש מנקמה

claims.text: לפי דיווח של וול סטריט ג'ורנל, ישראל סיפקה בחשאי במשך כמה שנים סיוע למורדים סורים בגולן.

claims.quote: הציניקנים יגידו שהשתמשנו בסבל שלהם", מתאר דרור, "אבל בחרנו להשקיע בזה משאבים ולסכן חיים למען סיוע הומניטרי

claims.quote: He has been in the hospital for two years, after having had his head and an eye practically rebuilt.

claims.quote: the years-long humanitarian activity has seen the treatment of some 7,000 Syrian children in a field hospital which has been operating over the last year.

claims.quote: More than 4,000 Syrians have been brought into Israel to receive medical treatment.

claims.text: לפי יאיר גולן, בחמש השנים שלאחר מכן טיפלו הכוחות ביותר מ-4,000 פצועים סורים.

claims.text: לפי גורמים רשמיים, כמעט שלושה רבעים מהפצועים שטופלו בישראל הם גברים בגיל לחימה, והשאר נשים וילדים.

claims.quote: According to the army, approximately half of those treated have been children, one-third were men, and the remaining 17 percent were women.

quote_translations.c80: This quote belongs to Lieutenant Colonel (res.) Eyal Dror, who headed the “Good Neighbor” directorate during the Syrian civil war
quote_translations.c67: Over 3500 war wounded, among them men, women and children, were transferred for treatment in Israel since 2013
quote_translations.c79: Israel, for its part, had to quickly get used to a new situation created in this war - a border on whose other side are some 250 thousand people
quote_translations.c68: Since the outbreak of fighting in Syria, there has been a severe shortage of medical infrastructure, doctors and medicines on the Syrian side of the border
quote_translations.c53: They simply came one night and put six stretchers at the fence
quote_translations.c54: I tried to advance this with the then Chief of Staff Benny Gantz, and was refused
quote_translations.c55: At first, in light of the opposition of the political echelon, Gantz personally approved bringing in the wounded - except for isolated cases
quote_translations.c59: There were some who managed to learn a little Hebrew, and they mainly said thank you and expressed appreciation for having been saved
quote_translations.c56: This concerns some 1,400 children from the age of one month to the age of 15, who were usually accompanied by a family member
quote_translations.c69: Since June 2016 the Good Neighbor directorate transferred to refugees from the war in Syria: 1524 tons of food, 947,520 liters of fuel for heating and for operating generators to produce electricity
quote_translations.c63: Many of them said to me ‘we thought you were the devil, and here you are saving lives’
quote_translations.c64: He was a Muslim, inside a Jewish synagogue, who simply sat and listened to me lecture
quote_translations.c61: They all declared that they had fought against the Assad regime, but we had no way of knowing how true this was
quote_translations.c60: We received an instruction to protect them from Druze, because some of them had fought Druze in Syria and there was a fear of revenge
quote_translations.c58: The cynics will say that we used their suffering”, Dror describes, “but we chose to invest resources in this and to risk lives for humanitarian aid
quote_translations.c62: However, with Assad’s renewed takeover of the area in 2018, the activity of the directorate came to an end
quote_translations.c57: Life-saving treatments were given to some 4,500 men, women and children, while alongside them some 7,000 more were treated at the field clinic
quote_translations.c66: At the Mazor Ladach field clinic, which the IDF set up together with an international aid organization in the southern Golan Heights, some 6,000 patients have been treated since its opening in August 2017
quote_translations.c52: led to the forces treating more than 4,000 wounded Syrians over the following five years
